reading: Two colours, two objects each. Each colour becomes its own column, starting at the bottom row: the colour whose leftmost cell is further left goes at col 0, and the other colour starts one column past the first column's width. Within a column, objects are left-aligned and stacked upward with a 1-row gap, the object that started further left at the bottom.

slots.groups: objects grouped by colour, groups ordered by leftmost x
slots.order: inside a group, by leftmost x (leftmost lowest)
slots.layout: bottom-aligned stacks with a 1-row vertical gap, columns separated by 1 empty column

why: every object keeps its shape and colour; the output holds exactly the input's objects, packed into bottom-left stacks

reading: A 3x3 grid of 5x5 panels split by background lines. One panel holds the full pattern and every other panel holds one directional piece of it. Each panel is moved to the slot matching the piece it shows (top-left piece to the top-left slot, and so on), and the full pattern goes to the centre.

slots.full: the panel whose pattern contains all the others
slots.target slot: for each panel, the position of its marked cells inside the full pattern (centre for the full one)

why: the output's panels are a permutation of the input's panels, and every panel's content agrees with its slot's region of the full pattern

reading: The grid splits into panels along full separator lines, each panel holding 3x3 blocks. In a panel crossed by a 4-line, the blocks swap places across that line. In a panel with no 4-line, the colour-1 blocks take the colour of the panel's single non-1 block.
verb: per panel: swap across 4-line or recolour 1-blocks

slots.scale: panels cut by full separator lines of the panel colour (5, 7, 9)
slots.case A: panel has an internal line of 4 -> swap the block halves across it
slots.case B: no 4-line -> recolour every 1 block to the panel's other block colour

why: separators and 4-lines never change; each panel is either the swap across its 4-line or the 1->other recolouring

reading: A periodic 0/1/2 lattice carries a few 8 overlays. Each 8 overlay is copied onto every other place where the lattice beneath it is the same, so its local underlying pattern repeats.
verb: replicate overlay at matching lattice positions

slots.anchors: every position whose underlying lattice window equals the window under the original overlay
slots.underlying: lattice recovered from identical rows/columns elsewhere

why: every added 8 lies on a cell whose underlying colour equals the colour under the original 8s (2 in pairs 0 and 2, 1 in pair 1), at positions that repeat the original's lattice context
invariants: all non-8 lattice cells away from copies

reading: Some rows contain a 1 followed by an 8. The cells strictly between the 1 and the 8 are cut out, and these strips are stacked top to bottom in row order.

slots.rows: input rows containing both a 1 and an 8
slots.segment: cells strictly between the 1 (left) and the 8 (right)
slots.assembly: segments stacked vertically in row order (all the same length)

why: each output row equals the between-1-and-8 segment of the k-th marked input row; the segments can sit in different columns, so this is no single box cut

reading: Each partial plus of 2s, whose arms are equal length (2 in most pairs, 3 in the last), is completed to a full plus. The missing cells are painted 8, and arms that run off the grid are clipped.

slots.subject: each partial 2-coloured plus
slots.size: arm length implied by the visible 2s (same for all pluses in a grid)
slots.paint: 8 on the plus cells that are not already 2

why: after painting, the 2/8 cells are exactly a union of equal-armed pluses, and every original 2 stays 2
invariants: all cells outside the completed pluses

reading: Each 6-coloured shape takes the colour of its nearest single marker. The recoloured shapes are cropped to their 4x4 boxes and concatenated, side by side if they are spread horizontally, stacked if vertically, in spatial order.
verb: recolour shapes by nearest marker and concatenate

slots.subject: the 6-coloured objects
slots.key: colour of the nearest isolated marker cell
slots.assembly: cropped boxes joined along the axis the shapes are spread on, in left-to-right or top-to-bottom order

why: each output block is one 6-shape's box with 6 replaced by its nearest marker's colour; the markers themselves are dropped

reading: A diagonal (up-right) segment of 2s of length n is erased and redrawn as a segment of length n+1 on the same diagonal. The new segment starts at the cell just past the old segment's upper end.
verb: advance diagonal and grow by one

slots.subject: the anti-diagonal 2-segment
slots.new start: first cell beyond the old upper-right end, continuing up-right

why: the output segment lies on the input segment's diagonal, is one longer, and touches the old segment's end without overlapping it

reading: The single 8 shape is a template. Every placement of that template, under any rotation (no reflection), that lands entirely on colour-3 cells has those cells repainted 8.
verb: find rotated template copies and paint them
why: the changed cells are exactly the union of all placements of a rotated template that lie entirely on 3s (checked on all 4 pairs)
invariants: all cells not covered by a match

reading: Exactly one object contains an 8 cell. The output is that object's box, with the 8 replaced by the object's own colour.
verb: crop marked object and heal it
why: the output is the 3x3 box of the only multi-coloured component, and its single 8 cell takes the colour of the surrounding shape
